extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists (readers of the Royal Society, 17th century)
extracted.subtask_description: A 17th‑century experimental report describing stepwise laboratory experiments (pneumatic/air‑pump studies, observational reports in astronomy and medicine) with observations, apparatus descriptions, and comparative discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a detailed stepwise experimental procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the exact sequence of operations and apparatus used (e.g. 'On putting a piece of shining rotten wood... into the receiver of a pneumatic engine or air-pump, and the pump being set to work...' — followed by numbered 'Exper. 1', 'Exper. 2', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each experiment is reported with the setup and the actions performed (placing specimen, exhausting air, letting air in, sealing pipes). Use numbered experiment entries and describe apparatus, manipulations, and immediate observations so readers can follow and reproduce the steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record quantitative details and timings precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Report counts and timing of operations and durations (e.g. 'during the five or six first exsuctions... about the seventh suck... about the tenth exsuction', 'we stayed above a quarter of an hour', 'full half an hour', 'twenty-four hours', '48 hours').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the number of pump strokes/exsuctions, elapsed times that phenomena persisted or returned, and any other numerical measures to allow temporal replication and assessment of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose and report appropriate specimens and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the type and size of specimens used (e.g. 'All these experiments were made with whitings, being the fittest kind for such trials.'; pieces 'above an inch long', 'size of a groat', 'larger than the former').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State why particular specimens were chosen (fitness for trial) and record their dimensions and condition, since specimen type/size affects outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary and control experimental variables (air density, compression, immersion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the phenomena under different conditions and report their effects (e.g. rarefaction by exhausting air, compression via a compressing instrument, immersion in water: 'The rarefaction of the air having so notable an effect...'; 'placing... in a glass... half filled with fair water').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly manipulate environmental/physical variables (vacuum level, compression, presence of water, sealing) and report how each variable alters the observed phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sealed/isolated apparatus to distinguish effects of contained air
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ hermetic sealing or confined pipes to test whether internal air sustains the phenomenon (e.g. 'we caused a piece of shining wood to be hermetically sealed up in a pipe of clear and thin glass... the wood retained its light'; 'Having hermetically sealed up a small piece... it was exhausted of air, and afterwards let in again').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sealing methods and small‑scale enclosed setups to determine whether an internal pocket of air or external air exchange is responsible for the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat trials and vary specimen size to assess robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform multiple trials and use specimens of different sizes to observe consistency (e.g. repeating the trial 'the following night' with a larger piece, experiments 11 and 12 with larger/smaller pieces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report outcomes across repetitions and sizes, noting any differences in time to extinguish, recovery on readmission of air, or persistence of light, to evaluate reproducibility and scale effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include comparative analysis with known analogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the observed phenomenon to better-known phenomena to highlight similarities and differences (explicit section: 'Comparison between burning Coal and shining Wood' listing five resemblances and six differences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use systematic comparison to known cases (e.g. burning coal) to help interpret mechanism, enumerating both resemblances and distinguishing features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe apparatus construction and procedural tricks that affect results
rubrics_metrics.description: Give constructional details and clever techniques used (e.g. cylindrical glass tube sealed at one end with quicksilver trap to alter internal air; use of small clear receivers to detect earlier dimming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report special apparatus arrangements (mercury column, inverted tubes, wedging specimens with cork) that materially affect internal pressures and thus observations, so readers can reproduce conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report observations with cautious, qualified interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame inferences with caution and limit claims to what the experiments support (e.g. 'which shows that the motion of such bodies as the particles of light may be freely made in vacuo, at least such a vacuum as the engine produces'; 'Mr. Boyle some suspicions he had about the possible causes...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating conclusions; indicate hypotheses, possible causes, and the limits of the apparatus' ability to settle the question, inviting further tests.
